summary.headline: Share India Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 48% YoY to Rs 124.41 crore on revenue of Rs 448 crore; management targets ~20% growth this year.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's strongest quarterly performance to date despite SEBI derivatives curbs and RBI funding restrictions on prop desks. Standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 349 crore and PAT rose 32% to Rs 90.85 crore; consolidated revenue rose 31% to Rs 448 crore and PAT rose 48% to Rs 124.41 crore, with consolidated PAT up 114% QoQ. Growth was attributed to MTF lending income, new subsidiaries (Share India Cred, GIFT City), PMS launch and merchant banking. Management plans CP and NCD issuance to offset funding constraints.

financial_highlights.value: Rs ~74 crore across six issues; EBITDA Rs 1.08 crore; PAT Rs 40 lakh

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Management said prop contributes ~52% of profitability and ~48% from broking; on revenue, prop is ~58-60%. Client volume is ~60% versus prop ~40%.

segments.name: MTF lending
segments.commentary: MTF book ~Rs 470 crore at end Q1, targeted at Rs 1,000 crore in two years; management called MTF the main source of sustainable interest income.

segments.name: PMS / wealth
segments.commentary: PMS AUM Rs 150 crore at end Q1 (launched in Q1); target ~Rs 250 crore by year-end. Wealth distribution team hiring, operations targeted from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt trading)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 under Keshav Goyal; ~Rs 74 crore underwritten/sold across six issues, PAT Rs 40 lakh.

segments.name: GIFT City / IFSC
segments.commentary: Turned positive in Q1 with ~Rs 2 crore of income per management, after prior losses.

segments.name: Institutional and merchant banking
segments.commentary: Active institutional clients 212 versus 186 at Q4 (+15%). Merchant banking completed a main-board IPO raising Rs 167 crore (subscription above 12x) and one SME IPO of ~Rs 200 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects ~20% growth in the current financial year, subject to market conditions.
Target of 25-30 new Tier-3 branches over 24 months; seven opened recently (six in Banaras, Indore, Bhopal, Raipur, Agra, Nagpur plus Hyderabad cluster).
Branch economics: each branch targets Rs 15 crore MTF book within ~8 months to break even; branches not profitable after 12 months to be shut.
AIF launch expected in Q3 FY27 pending regulatory approval; wealth distribution operations also targeted from Q3 FY27.
PMS AUM target ~Rs 250 crore by financial year end.
Plans to issue commercial paper (rated Crisil A1+) and NCDs to diversify funding; CP programme initiated.
capex_capacity: Seven new branches opened recently against a 30-branch target over two years; branches rolled out in tranches of about eight.

Acquisition of Enshrine (property-holding company, up to Rs 45 crore consideration) to secure ~18,000 sq ft carpet-area office in Mumbai (Interface 11 area); management cited property value above Rs 42 crore.
Silverleaf (HFT technology firm) acquisition previously announced; expected to add technology stack and HFT protocols and support geographic expansion.
AI, automation and in-house platform Techyon cited as technology investments.
demand_pricing: Management said realisations improved during the quarter and commodity business showed improvement.
Industry headwinds cited: SEBI F&O regulatory tightening and RBI curbs on prop-desk top-desk funding; management said smaller brokers face difficulty meeting higher capital requirements.
Retail MTF demand in Tier-3 cities described as underserved, with limited broker options for MTF.
Mid and small-cap volatility affected MTF book; management said it held its numbers with mild growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback period for Tier-3 branches given lower ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said each branch should reach break-even in ~8 months by building a Rs 15 crore MTF book; branches not profitable after 12 months will be closed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock underperforming despite low PE and high growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, attributing it to industry regulatory consolidation and cited diversification, institutional clients and subsidiaries as positives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of acquiring Silverleaf, the tech company?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Silverleaf (founded by IIT Bombay graduates, 12+ years in business) brings a technology stack and HFT protocols, supporting third-country expansion and back-end technology.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking and trading performance and what is the prop vs broking split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business has shifted toward lending via MTF (~Rs 465-470 crore) and fee streams from PMS, MF distribution and third-party products; prop contributes ~52% of profit and broking ~48%.

qa_highlights.question: Why pay up to Rs 45 crore for Enshrine, a company with Rs 2-3 crore turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Shah said the acquisition is mainly to obtain a Mumbai property (~18,000 sq ft carpet area, valued above Rs 42 crore) to consolidate Mumbai offices.

qa_highlights.question: Is prop still a very high share of total revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said prop was ~58-60% of revenue and ~52% of profit now, versus ~85-90% of revenue and ~70-75% of profit 8-9 years ago.

risks_watch: Prop trading still ~52% of profit and ~58-60% of revenue, exposed to SEBI derivatives rules and RBI prop-desk funding curbs.
Funding transition: CP and NCD programmes not yet issued; funding costs and timing are open.
Regulatory approval pending for AIF launch (targeted Q3 FY27).
Stock underperformance despite strong earnings; management attributed this to sector consolidation and external factors.
Q1 benefited from merchant-banking IPOs and valuation gains; sustainability of these flows is not assured.
Branch expansion carries execution risk; management set a hard stop at 12 months for loss-making branches.
Enshrine acquisition value (up to Rs 45 crore) and Silverleaf integration: limited disclosure on rationale and financials.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on results, calling Q1 the strongest to date, but defensive when questioned on prop dependence and the share price. Answers were sometimes inconsistent on prop-share figures, with management correcting an analyst on revenue versus profit split.
key_quotes: Despite this industry -wide headwinds, I am pleased to share that Share India has delivered its strongest quarterly financial performance to date.
Subject to overall market condition, we remain confident of delivering around 20% growth during the current financial year.
So, our goal is 8 months branch should be at par within 8 months.
In terms of distribution, our current prop to distribution is in what has been our average of around 52% is from prop and around 48% is from the broking business.
And if some branches are not profitable, even after 12 months, then there is a hard stop after 12 months.

adds.what: Tier-3 branch rollout: 25-30 new branches over 24 months (seven opened recently)
PMS AUM target ~Rs 250 crore by FY27 end (from Rs 150 crore)
Enshrine acquisition (up to Rs 45 crore) to secure ~18,000 sq ft Mumbai office

growth.why: Management guides to around 20% growth this FY and Q1 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY with PAT up 48%, but growth is tied to market conditions, the MTF book shows only mild growth, and the 25-30 branch rollout is a 24-month plan with no capacity utilisation disclosed.
